t: In front of you is the statue of Sir Joshua Reynolds, standing in the Annenberg Courtyard of Burlington House, just off Piccadilly. Reynolds was the first president of the Royal Academy, which occupies the main wing of this building, so he stands at home. He was a portrait painter, and he promoted what he called the Grand Style. George III knighted him in 1769. The sculptor was Alfred Drury, a leading figure in the New Sculpture movement, who also made figures on the Old War Office in Whitehall and on Vauxhall Bridge.
